body: Hm, actually nested classes in protocols are not supported (also one will be able to mimic it with a protocol field when https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/4536 will be fixed). Anyway, we definitely should not crash.

Thanks, the nested class was in there as a vestige of some refactoring. It took a little while to figure out what was going on because the error doesn't present when running the Protocol subclass through mypy only when you process something with a call to a function using it. So I thought it was worth fixing as other than the mention of "is_protocol_implementation" in the traceback it's not at all clear where to look for the problem.

issue.title: Use pluggy to allow plugin architecture for custom rules

repository.name: sqlfluff
repository.description: A modular SQL linter and auto-formatter with support for multiple dialects and templated code.

issue.body:
# Using pluggy to allow plugin architecture for custom rules (initially)

Resolves #164 

This PR changes sqlfluff to allow custom rules to be plugged through [pluggy](https://pypi.org/project/pluggy/). I think the same system could be used for dialects.

I added an example of a plugin.

Notes: 
* I changed the naming convention for rule classes to be `Rule_<PluginName: optional>_LXXX` so plugin maintainers don't have to worry about rule codes clashing.
* I added a way for users to include a default configuration for the plugin rules.
* I didn't use a different `RuleSet` for the new rules, I just register the plugin rules to the same RuleSet. Is there any advantage in having multiple RuleSets? I see that the current RuleSet is instantiated with the name "standard" which suggests there would be multiple RuleSets?

TODO:

- [x] Find a better example custom rule (any idea?).
- [x] Resolve the [cyclic dependency](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/compare/master...dmateusp:dmateusp/pluggy_for_rules?expand=1#diff-24adf7a8bcdebb4806459eba75db5ded6f952fac149d885a5d440d9e1840d716R343) between config and plugin_manager better (help?)
- [x] Find a good way to expose our test tooling to plugin maintainers (so they can test rules through the YAML system) (help?)
- [x] Add documentation (help?)
